subject: Business
title: Flywheel Effect: Momentum Builds on Itself
description: A 60-second lesson on Flywheel Effect: Momentum Builds on Itself.

hook.text: Amazon's flywheel: lower prices attract more customers, which attract more sellers, which lower prices further.

buildup.text: Jim Collins described the flywheel: each push adds energy. After many pushes, momentum becomes self-sustaining.

discovery.text: There's no single defining push. It's the accumulation of consistent actions in the same direction.

twist.text: Most companies never build flywheel momentum because they keep changing direction every quarter.

climax.text: Amazon printed its flywheel on a napkin in 2001. They've been spinning it the same way for 25 years.

punchline.text: Consistency in one direction beats brilliance in many.

quiz.question: What is the flywheel effect?
options: Consistent actions compound until momentum becomes self-sustaining
A sudden breakthrough that transforms a business
Spinning off subsidiaries to create value

details.summary: The flywheel effect, described by Jim Collins, shows how a series of good decisions and actions compound over time, building unstoppable momentum. Each turn of the flywheel builds on previous work, and after enough consistent effort, the system accelerates under its own momentum.
details.whyItMatters: The flywheel explains how companies like Amazon built compounding advantages. Understanding your flywheel reveals which activities create self-reinforcing growth loops and where consistent investment produces accelerating returns.
takeaways: Consistent effort in the right areas creates self-reinforcing momentum
Each turn of the flywheel builds on the energy stored from previous turns
Amazon's flywheel links lower prices to more customers to more sellers

faq.question: How does Amazon's flywheel work in practice?
faq.answer: Lower prices attract more customers. More customers attract more third-party sellers. More sellers increase selection and competition, enabling lower prices. Greater volume improves logistics efficiency, further reducing costs. Each element feeds the next in an accelerating cycle.

faq.question: How do you identify your company's flywheel?
faq.answer: Map the sequence of activities where each step enables the next. Look for loops where output from one activity becomes input for another. Test whether investing more in any single step accelerates the entire cycle. The flywheel should feel natural to your business model.
